id.description: The app in the API, assigned by the cloud and stable for the life of the app. Everything app-scoped takes this as its `:id`.

org_id.description: The organisation that owns this app. Every developer route is already scoped to the caller's org, so this confirms what a client is looking at rather than being a filter it applies.

name.description: The display name, shown in the console and available to the developer's own pages through the `app.name` mail-template variable. Free text, changed through `PATCH /api/apps/:id`.

identifier.description: The stable handle a client sends at login, lowercase and underscore-separated. **Globally unique, not per organisation** — `clientLoginRequest` carries no org context, so a collision is refused with `identifier_taken`.

robot_ids.description: The robots this app may reach, each referenced individually. Tags never grant rights, and a robot absent from this list is invisible to the app. What a user of the app may use on an attached robot follows that robot's `fleetless.yaml` and the organization's defaults, less what the app locks.

anyOf.patternErrorMessage: A role key is lower-case: it starts with a letter and continues with letters, digits and underscores, up to 63 characters in all — `operate`, `night_shift`. A capital, a dash, a dot, a space or a leading digit is refused, and `defaults` is reserved.

default_role.description: The role, by key, that an app user gets when created, invited or self-registered without an explicit one. `null` means this app has not chosen a default, the normal state of an app until someone picks one, and then a create or invite that names no role is refused. An invitation resolves the role when issued, so changing this never re-aims an outstanding one. The key is shown as stored and may name no role, which grants nothing; `GET /api/apps/:id/access` warns about it. It is set by `PUT /api/apps/:id/access`, not by `PATCH /api/apps/:id`.

created_at.description: When the app was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `GET /api/apps` orders by this field.

apps.description: Every app of the caller's organisation, oldest first by `created_at`. The org scope is the whole filter — there is no id to narrow by and nothing to refuse.
